What actually happens when you get brain freeze?
Most people think the cold is freezing your brain.
But your brain can't even feel pain.
When something ice-cold hits the roof of your mouth, the blood vessels there tighten up.
Then they suddenly swell back open, and a nerve panics.
It sends a pain signal, but your brain gets confused and thinks it's coming from your forehead.
To stop it, press your tongue against the roof of your mouth.
The warmth makes it go away faster.
